I took an appointment every time I visited, yet the doctor always seemed to be in a hurry and carried a very negative approach. There are two kinds of professionals: one who tells the truth while still motivating the patient to believe in recovery, and another who only talks in terms of giving up. As an athlete, hearing statements like “you will never be able to work out again” and “you will damage your body completely” was extremely demotivating. What made it worse was that my MRI showed two findings, but the doctor only noticed one—the second issue had to be pointed out by me during the next visit. This reflected a lack of attentiveness.

By God’s grace and with guidance from other competent and positive doctors, I am now healthy, fit, and doing everything I used to do. According to this doctor’s outlook, that would have been impossible—which clearly wasn’t the case. I also consulted a very renowned specialist who explained that everything was manageable and could be resolved.

A small piece of advice: a doctor should always speak the truth, but with hope and responsibility. Patients come seeking guidance, not hopelessness. To anyone reading this if you feel demotivated, do not lose heart. Take a second or even third opinion. The right doctor can make a world of difference.
